page: Amazon Web Services i4i.metal is a storage-optimized bare-metal server utilizing x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with Intel Xeon 8375C processors, providing a total of 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. The system operates at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz and features 1024.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage consists of 30,000 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. The network interface supports a baseline bandwidth of 75 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 125,019.7 and a PassMark CPU score of 87,524.92, both placing in the top 10% of tested servers. Single-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1,909.5 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1,678.0, both falling in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth is strong, recording 338.82 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 132.78 GB/sec for large-block write operations. In database-specific testing, the server achieved a PassMark database operations score of 30,569.9 and processed 109.81 million Redis SET operations per second, placing both metrics in the top 25%.

The hardware profile offers high resource density, combining massive local NVMe storage with a high-capacity memory array and dedicated compute resources. While single-threaded performance is average, the multi-threaded capabilities and high-speed local storage provide qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require high IOPS and low-latency data access. The server is suited for large-scale databases, data warehousing, transactional databases, and high-throughput web serving.
